about: Ledger of bugs: fixed, open, and claims checked and found not to be bugs. Source of docs/bugs.md and docs/bugs.html (python tools/bugs_page.py). Every fix PR adds or updates an entry here.

fields.origin: old = also in lcogtsnpipe (inherited); new = only in snpipe; ops = run scripts / infrastructure
fields.effect: measured effect on the SN 2024pxl reduction, or why there is none

bugs.title: Difference-image magnitudes use the wrong airmass in the extinction correction
bugs.where: mag.py image_table (old: lscdiff.py copies the science row; calibratemag.py uses its airmass)
bugs.what: A difference image normalized to the template (PHOTNORM=t, the default) is in the template's flux scale. Its zero point is measured on the template's stars (the template sn2 header: template airmass and site), but the extinction correction of the SN used the science frame's airmass and site, copied into the diff's database row.
bugs.why: The atmosphere term only cancels when both steps use the same image. Otherwise every point is off by k_template*X_template - k_science*X_science, e.g. ogg0m455-sq30-20240725-0178 (B): 0.23*1.617 - 0.21*1.049 = +0.15 mag too faint.
bugs.fix: mag reads airmass and site from the sn2 header that zcat used, so both steps always refer to the same image. Unsubtracted frames are unaffected (their header and row agree).
bugs.effect: Applied to the 2024pxl run (new_run, 2026-10-02): difference light curve points move -0.150 to +0.120 mag (median -0.022), 54 of 151 by more than 0.05 mag; unsubtracted 499/499 identical. Check against the unsubtracted magnitude of the same frame (calibrated correctly): before the fix the residual tracks the predicted error k_t*X_t - k_s*X_s (slope +0.62), after the fix it does not (slope -0.25); the correlation is weak (0.23) and the overall scatter is unchanged (0.037 -> 0.038), so the case rests mainly on the derivation. Because the old pipeline has the same bug, the published 2024pxl light curve probably carries it too.

bugs.title: getmag --type ph reports the PSF-fit error for the aperture magnitude
bugs.what: With --type ph the old code paired apmag with psfdmag.
bugs.why: The error belongs to a different measurement.
bugs.fix: Uses dapmag.
bugs.effect: Errors only; magnitudes unchanged.

bugs.title: getmag -o x.csv writes a space-separated table
bugs.what: The file named .csv was not CSV.
bugs.why: Tools reading it as CSV get one column.
bugs.fix: Real CSV, plus an ECSV with the frame name of every point.
bugs.effect: Format only.

bugs.title: Difference-image rows keep stale photometry of the science frame
bugs.what: The new row for the difference image is a copy of the science row, including its psfmag/mag/zero-point columns.
bugs.why: A later stage that skips a frame could report the unsubtracted value as the difference value.
bugs.fix: All photometry columns are reset on the difference row.
bugs.effect: None on 2024pxl (all columns were recomputed).

bugs.title: A failed SN PSF fit was exported as a precise measurement
bugs.what: When the fit did not converge its error was NaN, and max(0, NaN) stored it as 0. A fit that drifted far from the SN only raised a warning, and getmag did not look at psfmag QA.
bugs.why: A fit 57-10000 px from the SN measures something else; a zero error makes it look like the best point of the night.
bugs.fix: An undefined error is stored as missing (9999); a fit more than 2 FWHM from the SN position fails QA (good fits: median 0.9 px, 90th percentile 1.8 px); getmag drops points whose PSF fit failed when the magnitude comes from the PSF fit. Aperture magnitudes are measured at the aperture centroid and are not affected.
bugs.effect: Applied to 2024pxl: the 16 frames re-fitted and all 16 now fail psfmag QA (fits 15-318 px off the SN, 2.5-42 FWHM); they are no longer in lc_2024pxl_nodiff.csv (515 -> 499 points; the other 499 unchanged). They included two unflagged g points, lsc1m005-fa15-20241003-0063 (19.99 +- 0.005) and -0062 (19.34 +- 0.008), neighbours ~18.86, and one with dmag 8.3e7.

bugs.title: QA gates let NaN metrics pass
bugs.what: NaN compares False with every bound, so check('noise', NaN, hi=10) returned ok.
bugs.why: An undefined metric means the check could not be made.
bugs.fix: Non-finite metrics fail the gate.
bugs.effect: None found on 2024pxl (no gated metric was NaN).

bugs.title: Off-image catalog stars were re-centred onto the frame edge
bugs.what: IRAF keeps the input position of a star outside the image (OffImage); the port re-centred it onto the nearest edge pixels.
bugs.why: Hundreds of stars piled up in one place, formed one huge PSF-fit group and left junk rows in the star table.
bugs.fix: IRAF rule ported in both centroid functions.
bugs.effect: 247 of 566 frames had off-image stars; they were redone. Worst frames 900 s -> 60 s.

bugs.found_by: agent, comparing with IRAF on an edge frame
bugs.title: Aperture sky used a plain sigma clip instead of IRAF's 'mean' algorithm
bugs.what: IRAF first cuts the data range to min(mean-dmin, dmax-mean, 3 sigma); the port skipped that first pass.
bugs.why: Annuli reaching off-chip rows got a badly wrong sky.
bugs.fix: Exact IRAF first-pass rule.
bugs.effect: lsc1m004-fa03-20240818-0142: aperture correction -4.4 -> -0.078 (IRAF -0.073). PSF stage rerun on all frames.

bugs.found_by: agent, smoke test of the old pipeline on SN 2025rbs
bugs.title: APASS catalog written in sexagesimal instead of degrees
bugs.what: The port converted the coordinates in the wrong direction (old deg2HMS converts to degrees).
bugs.why: zcat cannot match stars; the old pipeline crashed on the file.
bugs.fix: Degrees, verified identical to the old-code APASS file of 2024pxl.
bugs.effect: None on 2024pxl (its catalog was made by the old code); would have broken every new target.

bugs.title: Pan-STARRS fallback did not run when SDSS returned nothing
bugs.what: An empty SDSS result is stored as '' and the fallback call treated '' as 'already done'.
bugs.why: Fields outside SDSS ended up with no g/r/i catalog.
bugs.fix: '' is retried with --force, or for the sloan field when Pan-STARRS is requested.
bugs.effect: None on 2024pxl or 2025rbs (both inside SDSS).

bugs.title: Worker processes reused the parent's SQLite connection
bugs.what: The connection cache was copied into forked workers.
bugs.why: SQLite connections must not cross fork(); concurrent writers can corrupt state or lock.
bugs.fix: A forked process opens its own connection (cache keyed on the process id).
bugs.effect: No corruption seen on 2024pxl.

bugs.found_by: agent (wcs stage crashed during the run)
bugs.title: One bad frame aborted the whole stage
bugs.what: An exception in one frame (sep pixel-buffer overflow) stopped the stage for all frames.
bugs.why: One frame must not stop a reduction.
bugs.fix: Per-frame exceptions become a 'fail' QA record; sep pixstack raised.
bugs.effect: The wcs stage on the 2024 science frames still has to be rerun (only the 18 templates were checked).

bugs.title: Test variants of a difference image overwrote the default image's QA
bugs.what: The zero-point-gain test run (.zp) wrote its QA file over the default diff's QA.
bugs.why: Light-curve filtering read the wrong verdict.
bugs.fix: Variants keep their own QA file; default selection skips .zp/.cut products.
bugs.effect: 27 QA files overwritten, restored from the summaries.

bugs.title: Template PSF is not transformed to the science pixel grid
bugs.what: The template is resampled onto the science grid, but PyZOGY gets the template PSF in native template pixels.
bugs.why: Different pixel scale (0.387 vs 0.74 "/px for 0.4 m science with a 1 m template) or rotation changes the effective PSF.
bugs.fix: Measure the PSF on the registered template (or transform it through the same registration).
bugs.effect: Not measured. Could matter for the 47 difference points from 0.4 m cameras.

bugs.title: PSF-fit errors on difference images ignore the subtracted sky and reference noise
bugs.what: Pixel variance = max(data,0)/gain + ron^2; on a sky-subtracted difference image that misses most of the noise. DAOPHOT's chi scaling is also missing.
bugs.why: PSF errors on difference images are underestimated.
bugs.fix: Pass the propagated difference variance, or scale errors by the reduced chi.
bugs.effect: Small: the difference light curve uses aperture magnitudes; unsubtracted PSF errors somewhat underestimated.

bugs.title: Grouped PSF fits have one sky per star instead of one per group
bugs.what: photutils sums the per-star sky terms of a group, so they are degenerate (DAOPHOT fits one group sky).
bugs.why: Rank-deficient fit; covariances of grouped stars are less reliable.
bugs.fix: One shared background parameter per group.
bugs.effect: None or small (the SN fit is a single source).

bugs.title: Zero point 'succeeds' when every calibration star is clipped
bugs.what: With no stars left, the initial guess is returned with zero error.
bugs.why: A made-up zero point looks exact.
bugs.fix: Fail when no calibrators are kept.
bugs.effect: None on 2024pxl (no zero point with zero error).

bugs.title: An automatic WCS refit can pass QA without being saved
bugs.what: Frames that start as good are opened read-only; a later refit is not written.
bugs.why: Downstream stages read the old WCS.
bugs.fix: Reopen in update mode when a refit is needed.
bugs.effect: None (no refits happened in this run).

bugs.title: --no-recenter does not fix the PSF-fit position
bugs.what: Only the starting position changes; x0/y0 stay free.
bugs.why: Forced photometry can drift to a neighbour.
bugs.fix: Fix x0/y0 in the fit when recentering is off.
bugs.effect: None (option not used).

bugs.title: SN stamp coordinates are wrong when the cutout is trimmed at the image edge
bugs.what: The stamp origin is computed from the requested size, not the actual cutout origin.
bugs.why: Background exclusion and reported psfx/psfy are offset near edges.
bugs.fix: Use the cutout's own origin in both directions.
bugs.effect: No magnitude effect found; psfx/psfy off by ~1-2 px.

bugs.title: Aperture pixel weights differ from IRAF
bugs.what: Geometric overlap instead of IRAF's linear ramp.
bugs.why: Not identical to IRAF, as docs/decisions.md claims.
bugs.fix: Port the IRAF ramp, or document the difference.
bugs.effect: < 1e-5 mag at the pipeline's 2-4 FWHM apertures.

bugs.title: Binning ignored when the pixel scale comes from CCDSCALE
bugs.what: The fallback ignores CCDSUM, unlike psf.pixscale().
bugs.why: Binned frames would get apertures twice too large.
bugs.fix: Use psf.pixscale().
bugs.effect: None (LCO frames have PIXSCALE).

bugs.title: Job scripts report success when stages fail, and can delete products after a failed copy
bugs.what: Scripts end with a logging command, so SLURM sees success; the old 2025rbs job marks the export done before copying and then removes scratch.
bugs.why: A dependent job can start on missing data; a 40 h run can lose its products.
bugs.fix: Check expected products, return non-zero on failure, keep scratch if the export fails.
bugs.effect: None so far (all 836 2025rbs frames are valid FITS).

bugs.title: Report claims stronger than the evidence
bugs.where: docs/decisions.md, docs/report/README.md, README.md, docs/index.html, tools/compare.py, tools/stage_report.py
bugs.what: 'Identical' aperture photometry (9 of 1,230 stars differ by > 0.01 mag, chip edge); headline diff agreement includes a QA-failed -3.94 mag point; '8.1 h -> 2.5 h' is a sum of stage timings with 2 stages estimated; 'WCS checked for every frame' (only 18 templates); paper comparison not reproducible (45 vs 113 matches now); ladder recoveries 19 vs 21 and inferred.
bugs.why: Readers would trust numbers that are not what they say.
bugs.fix: Reword with the real statistics, save frame manifests, plot the exported light curve.
bugs.effect: Documentation only.

bugs.title: zcat 'module-global keep'
bugs.what: A global statement inside an if.
bugs.why: In Python the global statement applies to the whole function, so it works as intended.

bugs.title: compare.py could pair different stars by row index
bugs.what: Old and new star tables are paired by row.
bugs.why: Checked: rows at the same index are the same star (positions agree to < 0.001 deg).
bugs.fix: Optional assertion on positions.
